1- Scope — Covers the dimensions, construction and testing of upholstery springs. 

2- Symbols — Following symbols are used in this standard ( see also figures in Tables 1 and 2): 

d = wire diameter, mm 
Di = maximum diameter of the spring, mm 
n 2 = minimum diameter of the spring, mm 

£0 = unloaded length of the spring, mm 
Lb = theoretical block length, mm 

n = number of turns 

3. Dimensions and Tolerances — Shall be as given in Tables 1 and 2.

IS: 7864 (Part I)- 1975 

3.1 Tolerance on Unloaded Length — Shall be ± 5 percent of the unloaded length L . 

3.2 Springs of sizes other than those mentioned in Tables 1 and 2 may be manufactured subject to 
agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 

4. Material — Upholstery springs shall be made from hard-drawn steel wire, patented and non- 
patented according to IS : 2589-1975 ' Specification for hard-drawn steel wire for upholstery springs 
(first revision ) '. 

5. Workmanship and Finish 

5.1 The springs may be phosphate coated, copper coated or galvanized according to IS: 4826-1968 
1 Galvanized coatings on round steel wires ' or coated with black stoving enamel paint. Any other 
protective coating may also be used subject to agreement between the purchaser and the manufac- 
turer. The coating shall be adherent. 

5-1-1 The copper plating, when springs are copper plated, shall not be less than 6 g/m 2 of the 
surface area. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Scragging — The spring shall be compressed to the theoretical block length L B three times in 
quick succession before any dimensions are measured. The theoretical block length shall be 
calculated as follows: 

L B = d x ( n + 1 ) 

6.1-1 Lb shall not be less than 6d in any case. 

6.2 Sample Size— Up to 5 percent samples of any size offered may be subjected to the compression 
test outlined in 6.3. Other sample sizes subject to agreement between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer may be selected. 

6.3 Compression Test — The upholstery springs shall be scragged 25 times as outlined in 6.1. 
After this there shall not be any perceptible permanent set and the spring shall not be out of 
straightness by more than 10 percent of the unloaded length, L . 

7. Designation — Shall include: 

a) Commonly used name; 

b) Form of spring; 

c) Wire diameter, d; 

d) Unloaded length, L ; 

e) Number of this standard; and 

f) Surface treatment 

Example-. 

An upholstery spring of Form A made from wire diameter d = 2'50 mm having 
unloaded length L = 220 mm and galvanized shall be designated as: 

Upholstery Spring A 2'50 X 220 IS : 7864 ( Part I ) Galvanized 

8. Marking — The package containing the springs shall be marked with: 

a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark and type number, 

b) Lot or batch number, 

c) Designation, and 

d) Quantity. 

8.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

3 



IS: 7864 (Part I)- 1975 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

These upholstery springs are used in the manufacture of bed spring units, mattresses, furniture- 
cushions, furniture spring units, automobile seats and back units, and railway seats and back units. 
There are two types of upholstery springs — conical type and flat type. Part I of this standard 
covers conical type and Part II flat type ( under preparation ). 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the following publications^ 
IRS-R31-61 Indian Railway Specification for springs, upholstery. 

TGL6450 (Blatt I )-1961 Polsterfedern — Taillenfeder 100 bis 360 mm lang, kegeffeder 80 bis- 
230 lang (Upholstery springs, conical and double conical) issued by Amt fur Standards 
sierung, Messwesen und waren Prufung. 



Printed at Neelkamal printers, Delhi, India
